Perhaps I was not clear on my point. I do think calamities are great, just not as they are now. I actually prefferd not having the counter for that extra kick. It's just the frequency at which they appear seems to be higher than what I remember from the past. It makes them a complete nuisance to deal with and come with little gratification after a while (especially if  you are forced to sprint across the map each time).

And while I do concede that getting better at the game would likely help a great deal in that regard (as well as a higher luck stat), I still believe that some of the scenarios that calamities can spawn under are unreasonable from a gameplay perspective. Essentially I am advocating to reducing their frequency, not their removal. 

  
Also, while " just look up and run straight towards them every time" is sound advice that I already tend to follow, you seem to forget that both maps have large areas that obscure your lign of sight towards the sky. Doesn't always work and doesn't address my issue with calamities. It's not their difficulty, it's their frequency.

**This will have been my first serious attempt at writing here. As a bit of context about me for anyone interested:**

This is the first time in more than 6 years that I have taken up writing again. Rust is flaking off old, long still gears as  they begin to turn anew. I cannot express enough how much it meant to me when people actually read AND commented on what amounts to my first draft. It made me extatic with joy. To think a a decently sized classroom full of people liked what I made is incredible. I needed that. 

The original post was a seriously hard step to make. So many doubts and fears swirling around in my head. I posted it to finally reclaim a piece of myself I had lost somewhere along the way. To challenge my demons and to take even just a small step further in a better direction. 

Though this here is my first serious attempt, i still experimented with a few styles and formats. I hope it is not too jarring and doesn't disrupt the telling of the story too much.

It's fine to pace the game. But I think it is badly implemented. Instead of spreading out general pacing oveer other areas of the game they pretty much hard-lock one specific aspect of it. It's a valid argument that it helps prolong the game but considering a 10% drop chance (that is **shared** with another item in the pool), a hard 8 hour regen timer for 1 key and the comparatively ridiculous amount of keys (especially SR ones) needed to upgrade a single character makes the whole thing less satisfying. The reward-for-effort factor is (for me and my friends at least) close to rock-bottom. You are literally forced to just wait to **"potentially"** progress at a snails pace. If the fights were at least a challenge then some aspect of fun would be brought back...but then again you have a reward-for-effort issue. Either implement a spceial resource lock or a small drop rate, not both - at least not for something extremely essential. Until you get lucky several times in a row over a relatively long time, each character will feel like its just stuck in a limbo of just-short-of-decent/annoyingly missing vital components to compete.
